text: The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to flow. It is the physical manifestation of a Tuesday afternoon that refused to end. When lit, the candle does not burn; rather, it apologizes to the darkness for being so bright, melting into a puddle of regret and paraffin. The wick is not a string, but a tiny, anxious ladder that the flame uses to climb out of its own shadow. If you listen closely, you can hear the wax weeping softly, not because it is hot, but because it realizes it is being consumed by the very light it was born to create. This is the paradox of illumination: to be seen, one must disappear.
